identity.description: Competition-proven simple forecaster (won M3, strong in M4): deseasonalize, then combine a linear-drift theta-line with an SES theta-line — equivalent to SES with drift on the deseasonalized series, reseasonalized. Near-zero tuning surface with accuracy that embarrasses far heavier methods on monthly/quarterly business series.

consumes.note: regular time-indexed numeric series; default multiplicative deseasonalization additionally wants strictly positive values

emits.note: point forecast + prediction_intervals() from the SES-with-drift form; the fitted alpha and drift are retrievable but carry no SEs, so no coefficients emit is claimed

period.note: seasonal cycle length s; inferred from the index frequency when null

deseasonalize.note: classical multiplicative decomposition before the theta lines; the seasonality test (use_test) can veto it

use_test.note: autocorrelation-based seasonality test that disables deseasonalization when seasonality is not significant — leave on

method.note: deseasonalization form; 'auto' picks multiplicative only for strictly positive series

invariances.why: SES-with-drift on a (de)seasonalized series is equivariant to rescaling; forecasts rescale with the input
a log transform swaps multiplicative for additive seasonal structure and changes what the linear drift means — a modeling choice
classical decomposition and the SES recursion both need a regular gap-free grid
single numeric series; no exogenous pathway of any kind
prediction intervals assume Gaussian SES innovations, and multiplicative deseasonalization presumes stable positive seasonal ratios
the seasonality test and classical decomposition need >=2 full cycles; below that theta silently degrades to plain SES-with-drift — acceptable but no longer seasonal
the drift term extends the fitted linear trend of the deseasonalized series indefinitely — theta's whole edge over pure SES, and its long-horizon risk

featureStats.why: feeds the built-in seasonality test that decides whether deseasonalization runs at all; borderline strength is where theta's auto-test flips behavior
the drift theta-line is half the method — a real slope is where theta beats SES/naive, no slope means the drift term just adds variance
family gate: the seasonality test is unreliable under 2 complete cycles, so seasonal handling must be forced off rather than trusted
multiplicative deseasonalization (the default) is undefined at non-positive values — this stat forces method='additive' or disables deseasonalization

modelMetrics.why: the family's honest scoreboard, and theta's historical claim to fame — it won M3 on exactly this kind of relative-accuracy ranking against far more complex entrants

edgeCases.behavior: decomposition raises or produces invalid seasonal factors

edgeCases.condition: series shorter than 2 full seasonal cycles

edgeCases.behavior: invalid frequency for decomposition and recursion

driver.constructor: ThetaModel(endog, period=s, deseasonalize=True, use_test=True).fit(); forecast(horizon) / prediction_intervals(horizon)
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon); positivity check to pick deseasonalization method; forecast + prediction_intervals merged into one frame

placementClaims.why: decomposition and SES recursion need a gap-free regular grid; time-aware interpolation, never tabular median
log transform turns multiplicative seasonality additive and makes the drift a growth rate — often the better-behaved space for business series
single numeric series has nothing to encode
